tasks.short: Discuss equipment faults and repairs with customers.

steps.what: Open the actual customer work order and equipment service history
Ask about actual symptoms and explain the actual repair and its limitations
outputs: actual customer discussion and clarified symptoms

steps.what: Enter and check actual symptoms and explanations in the work-order fields
inputs: actual customer discussion and clarified symptoms

tasks.design: Configure native {HELPDESK} asset-history links for the actual customer conversation. Keep questioning, repair explanations and actual work-order entry human; existing structured fields already suffice for this brief note.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated navigation from customer to asset history.
tasks.still_hard: Clarifying intermittent symptoms and setting accurate expectations.
tasks.human_edge: Listen and explain actual findings understandably.
tasks.altitude: Less lookup during customer discussion; repair judgement unchanged.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native field-service asset links reduce history navigation without replacing customer questioning or explanations.

assumptions: Boundary includes conversation and its actual work-order entry. Dispatcher/customer provides actual asset ID and complaint; prior technicians produce real service records. Technician resolves missing asset matches manually in s1 and captures actual clarified symptoms in s3. No inferred fault, invented transcript or new compulsory note baseline.

tasks.short: Instruct customers in safe equipment use.

steps.what: Find the correct equipment model's current safe-use instructions
Demonstrate actual equipment controls and safety precautions and answer customer questions
outputs: actual safe-use instruction and customer response

steps.what: Record and check actual instruction given and unresolved customer questions
inputs: actual safe-use instruction and customer response

tasks.design: Link actual asset models to current manufacturer {DOCS} instructions in {HELPDESK}. Technician demonstrates real controls and safety practices and records actual instruction afterwards; retrieving a manual does not prove customer understanding.
tasks.still_hard: Teaching safe operation on the customer's actual setup.
tasks.human_edge: Adapt explanation and check actual customer understanding.
tasks.altitude: Less manual lookup; safety instruction unchanged.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native asset-document links reduce manual lookup without replacing equipment demonstrations or establishing customer competence.

assumptions: Boundary is actual instruction and existing service note. Manufacturer supplies model, revision and instructions; technician checks actual model in s1, manually finds missing instructions and captures actual instruction outcomes in s3. No generated safety text or inferred completed instruction.

tasks.short: Read and interpret audiovisual technical documentation.

steps.what: Locate the correct model and revision of diagrams and service documentation
Read circuit and block diagrams and interpret actual signal paths and specifications
Annotate and check actual pin references and findings needed for the repair

tasks.design: Configure native {DOCS} model/revision filters and {HELPDESK} document links. Keep actual technical reading and diagram interpretation human; native annotation tools already cover the small written-reference step.
tasks.previous_blocker: Finding matching documentation among similar models and revisions.
tasks.still_hard: Understanding actual signal paths and device-specific behaviour.
tasks.human_edge: Apply circuit knowledge to the actual equipment.
tasks.altitude: Less document retrieval; technical understanding unchanged.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native model/revision indexing reduces document retrieval without interpreting electronic circuits.

assumptions: Boundary includes technical documentation reading and actual working annotations, not physical repair. Manufacturer supplies model, revision and document identity; technician verifies actual equipment and resolves missing matches manually in s1. Actual interpretation occurs in s2, annotations in s3. No free extracted circuit model.

tasks.short: Maintain work orders and test and maintenance reports.

steps.what: Collect actual completed work, test readings, parts and time information
Compile work orders and test and maintenance reports from actual service evidence
outputs: draft service record and test report

loop.purpose: Convert actual technician dictation into draft service fields
loop.input: actual service evidence and technician dictation
loop.output: draft fault/action narrative with exact test values and parts references
loop.check: Technician checks fault versus hypothesis, actual action, omitted tests, units, part identities and unsupported completion claims against evidence
loop.stop: Unknown part, absent test evidence or one failed retry requires manual entry
loop.why_not_simpler: Native fields and instrument import first; variable technician narrative needs bounded extraction

steps.what: Check the complete final work order and test report against actual service evidence
inputs: draft service record and test report
outputs: checked final service record and test report

steps.what: Commit the final service record and test report
inputs: checked final service record and test report
outputs: committed service record and test report

tasks.design: Test native {HELPDESK} work-order fields and {OTHER} test-instrument imports first. Use a bounded loop only for actual dictated service narrative, then technician checking of the complete final record before commit; no automatic repair completion or customer invoice is implied.
tasks.previous_blocker: Turning actual service findings into consistent written records.
tasks.enabler_now: Native field-service records plus bounded technician-note extraction.
tasks.still_hard: Distinguishing measured findings from suspected causes and unperformed tests.
tasks.human_edge: Document what was actually done and whether evidence supports it.
tasks.altitude: Less service-note composition; technical sign-off responsibility unchanged.

evidence.claim: FieldBuddy supports technician work orders, checklists and asset management; the bounded note-extraction extension is not established by this source.
Model knowledge: bounded extraction of actual technician dictation can draft service fields subject to meaning and source checks.

assumptions: Boundary is actual service records through commit, not physical repair, billing or customer sends. Technician produces actual fault observations, actions, asset ID, parts, hours and test readings; s1 collects actual evidence and s2 includes dictation, manual missing-field capture and draft correction within60 percent remaining. No free structured fault/cause labels or fabricated test results. Instrument import unavailable means manual entry.

Native first; already configured fields/imports earn zero saving. Provisional50 entry reduction applies only to actual repeated narrative composition; normal full-record QA24 and evidence collection25 remain. Commit1 retained; no new sign-off ceremony. Shares not measured.
unknowns: Actual narrative entry share and native work-order support
research_questions: Can extracted notes preserve unconfirmed faults and distinguish performed from planned tests?
